ExecutionPacket.purpose: Implement verified Thief support as the fifth player without regressing current four-player gameplay.
ExecutionPacket.contract-excerpt: M-VAST-THIEF-SUPPORT introduces Thief as a supported fifth-player faction and must keep four-player setups working.
ExecutionPacket.graph-entry-excerpt: M-VAST-THIEF-SUPPORT depends on rules/thief.xml plus the existing game, UI, serialization, bot, and host modules.

dependency-contract-summaries.dependency-1: `rules/thief.xml` is the semantic source of truth for Thief behavior.
dependency-contract-summaries.dependency-2: The game engine remains the authority for legal actions and state transitions.
dependency-contract-summaries.dependency-3: UI changes must not leak hidden information or break current supported factions.

ExecutionPacket.verification-excerpt: Run compile, browser bundle, five-player startup, and replay/simulation checks that include Thief.

notes.note-1: Workers should prove both new five-player behavior and non-regression of four-player flows.
Only list graph facts that changed in the implementation wave.

module-checks.command-3: Run a five-player startup and focused Thief scenario pass.
module-checks.command-4: Run host-side replay/simulation checks with Thief actions.

required-trace-assertions.assertion-1: Thief enablement must not break existing four-player setups.

wave-follow-up.item-1: Re-run browser interaction checks for any UI panel changed to support the fifth player.

phase-follow-up.item-1: Do not close the Thief phase until both five-player and four-player evidence are green.

FailurePacket.scenario: Five-player setup with Thief fails to start or diverges from the rules.

expected-evidence.assertion-1: Five-player setup succeeds and exposes only legal Thief actions.

observed-evidence.log-1: Observed startup validation failure or illegal Thief action set.
observed-evidence.trace-1: first divergent step in setup, render, serialization, or simulation path

FailurePacket.suggested-next-action: Read `rules/thief.xml`, inspect the setup and legal-action boundary, and apply the smallest fix that preserves four-player behavior.
